For individual clients

You can begin directly with your evaluation.

Neither consultation is required for individual care. Choose an optional conversation first, or go straight to the diagnostic evaluation (90791).

  1. Optional

    Talk before you begin

    A free 10-minute phone consultation offers a brief introduction. A paid 30-minute individual consultation gives you more time to discuss fit, questions, and the care process. Choose either, both, or neither.

  2. First clinical appointment

    Diagnostic evaluation (90791)

    Your clinician gathers information about your concerns, relevant history, needs, and goals. The evaluation helps clarify what is happening and provides the foundation for your treatment plan.

  3. Your ongoing care

    A measurable treatment plan

    Together, identify clear goals, an evidence-based approach suited to your needs, and how progress will be measured. Revisit the plan as you work, so appointments remain purposeful and responsive to your goals.

Request a diagnostic evaluation →Request a paid 30-minute individual consultation →

For couples

Start together. Understand each person. Return together.

All couples begin with a 30-minute couples consultation. You may have an optional free 10-minute phone consultation before it, but the phone call does not replace the required 30-minute consultation.

  1. 01 · Required first step

    30-minute couples consultation

    Meet with your couples therapist to discuss what brings you in, begin aligning goals, and agree on the rhythm and frequency of care. This is a paid consultation, separate from ongoing couples sessions.

  2. 02 · Each partner separately

    One diagnostic evaluation per partner

    Each partner has a separate, one-time diagnostic evaluation with the couples therapist. These appointments gather each person’s history, concerns, and perspective to help build a treatment plan that reflects both partners’ goals.

  3. 03 · Back together

    53-minute couples sessions

    Only after the 30-minute consultation and both partner evaluations are completed, return together for the initial 53-minute couples session and then ongoing couples sessions. Work from a shared, measurable treatment plan, using an evidence-based approach suited to your presenting concerns and reviewing progress along the way.

Do not request a 53-minute couples session before all three preparation appointments are complete: the 30-minute consultation and a separate evaluation for each partner. A 10-minute introduction is optional; you may schedule the 30-minute consultation directly. Existing individual clients follow this same couples pathway.

A couples therapist, not your ongoing individual therapist.

The separate diagnostic evaluations are part of the couples assessment. They do not establish ongoing individual therapy with your couples therapist. If you also need individual therapy, that care is with a separate individual therapist.

Discuss privacy, records, and how information from the individual evaluations is handled with your couples therapist before those appointments. The practice’s disclosure and consent process governs those arrangements.

Request a 30-minute couples consultation →

Couples consultations and couples sessions are private pay. Confirm the fees and any applicable coverage for diagnostic evaluations separately; this pathway does not establish insurance eligibility.

Available to all clients

What to expect from your 10-minute consultation.

This optional, free introduction is available to individual clients and couples. It is not a diagnostic evaluation or a therapy session. The calendar may reserve 15 minutes, but the consultation lasts 10 minutes.

Usually a phone call

These consultations are usually by phone. Occasionally, one is arranged through telehealth and you can join virtually using the access instructions provided for your appointment.

Phone is the immediate fallback

If the technology does not work immediately, the consultation will be a phone call instead. Keep your phone available and make sure your contact number in SimplePractice is current.

Expect a practice or hidden number

The call may display Marriage.Family.Therapy, or it may arrive from a hidden, private, or unknown number. Be ready to answer at your scheduled time.

The phone fallback described here applies to the 10-minute consultation. Confirm the format and any interruption plan for clinical appointments with your clinician.

Already receiving care?

Schedule your next appointment.

Use your existing SimplePractice Client Portal rather than starting a new-client request. After signing in, open Appointments and use Request appointment when available. A request is not confirmed until the practice accepts it.

Returning for individual care

Request the appointment type you have agreed on with your clinician. You do not need another introductory consultation to continue individual care.

Existing clients: schedule an appointment

If appointment requests or the correct service are not shown, contact your clinician or support. Do not choose a different appointment type just to reserve a time.

Returning for couples care

Do not schedule the initial or an ongoing 53-minute couples session until the 30-minute couples consultation and a separate diagnostic evaluation for each partner have been completed.

Already being an individual client, having a Client Portal login, or completing a 10-minute call does not replace these steps.

We have completed the consultation and both partner evaluations

Request your couples session through your existing Client Portal. If you are unsure whether the preparation is complete, confirm with your couples therapist first.

Consultation completed, but one or both partner evaluations still needed? Contact your couples clinician to arrange the remaining evaluation before requesting a joint session.

Requesting your appointment

Three practical steps to schedule.

  1. 01

    Clarify what you are looking for

    Choose individual or couples care using the paths above. You do not have to choose a therapy approach before contacting us.

    Explore services →
  2. 02

    Review clinician information

    Read the profiles and compare who each clinician works with, their focus areas, and their approach.

    Meet the team →
  3. 03

    Schedule

    In SimplePractice, choose the clinician, appointment type, and available time. Follow the confirmation and preparation instructions you receive. If the right appointment type is not listed, ask support before choosing a different service.

    Schedule in SimplePractice →

Common questions

A few practical answers.

Need help finding the right place to go? Start here.

Where do I request a consultation or appointment?

The consultation and appointment buttons open our SimplePractice scheduling options in the same tab. Choose the appointment type and clinician there. Appointment requests are not confirmations. If the correct appointment type is not available, contact support rather than selecting a different service.

How do I ask about insurance benefits?

Use the Verify benefits button to open an email to support@mft.care. Ask the support team how to begin a benefits check without including insurance numbers or clinical details in that initial message. A consultation or diagnostic evaluation does not guarantee insurance coverage.

Where do existing clients sign in?

Use the existing client portal for SimplePractice. The staff Operations link in the footer is separate from ordinary appointment scheduling.

Where can I find Marriage.Reset?

Choose Marriage.Reset in the top navigation. That page includes a separate sign-in link for Marriage.Reset clients.

Have a different question?

Contact the support team about the practice or how to get started.
